title: Integer-shift squares for normalized realization insertions
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. For finite-type $k$-schemes $W$ work on the small pro-etale sites with $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ and the strict semilinear system category $\mathscr S_W$ (module sheaves $M_n$ over $(A_n)_W$ with compatible semilinear transition maps). Use its ordinary unbounded derived category, derived reduction $\mathcal R_W$, total limit $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$, and actual adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ with unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. System operations are inverse image $P_v$ for separated finite-type maps $v$, direct image $S_p$ for proper $p$, quasi-compact open extension $J_j$, and derived tensor, with the integral counterparts of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Restrict input and intermediate systems to normalized systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude in common finite intervals; integral inputs are derived complete and constructible. Use the fixed slotwise cochain shifts of [def-pur-integral-operation-shift-data], with the signed second tensor slot, and the K-injective strict-tower Roos model for total limit. Write $\chi_H:H(M[r])\to H(M)[r]$ for a designated slot, holding other slots fixed. Let $d_A$ be the actual single-operation comparison of [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence], and let the canonical comparisons $c_V$ have the recursion of [lem-pur-integral-realization-recursion]. Define
$$a_A(M)=d_A(\mathcal LM)\circ(\mathcal LA(e_M))^{-1}:\mathcal LA(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\rm int}(\mathcal LM),$$
for unary $A$, and
$$a_\otimes(M,N)=d_\otimes(\mathcal LM,\mathcal LN)\circ\bigl(\mathcal L(e_M\otimes^Le_N)\bigr)^{-1}:\mathcal L(M\otimes^LN)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal LM\widehat\otimes^L\mathcal LN.$$
Then the inverse unit $u_K^{-1}:\mathcal L\mathcal RK\to K$, every $a_A$, and both designated-slot comparisons of $a_\otimes$ commute naturally with each integer shift: $\chi_{\rm target}\,a(M[r])=a(M)[r]\,\chi_{\rm source}$, with the analogous equation for $u_K^{-1}$. The comparisons here are exactly the composites of the fixed operation, reduction and Roos shift comparisons; they are coherent for addition of shifts, including zero and negative shifts. In particular these are squares for the actual normalized insertion maps, with the second-slot Koszul sign and the shifted-cone sign, rather than comparisons chosen by evaluating finite levels.

proof.text: The recursion lemma gives invertible actual $u_K,e_M$ and exactly the displayed insertion formulas. Thus $b_A=\mathcal LA(e_M)$ and $b_T=\mathcal L(e_M\otimes^Le_N)$ are invertible. Fix the operation, reduction and Roos comparisons of the shift-data definition. For a fixed integer $r$, write $s_F:F(Z[r])\to F(Z)[r]$ for their composite along a functor $F$; for a bifunctor fix one slot at a time.

proof.text: The reduction/limit shift-adjunction lemma gives the squares for the actual $u,e$, including the shifted Roos cone. In particular $s_{\mathcal L\mathcal R}u_{K[r]}=u_K[r]s_{\mathrm{id}}$. Multiplying on the left by $u_K^{-1}[r]$ and on the right by $u_{K[r]}^{-1}$ gives $s_{\mathrm{id}}u_{K[r]}^{-1}=u_K^{-1}[r]s_{\mathcal L\mathcal R}$, the required variable square.

proof.text: For unary $A$, put $D=\mathcal LA\mathcal R\mathcal L$, $X=\mathcal LA$, $Y=A_{\rm int}\mathcal L$, $b=\mathcal LA(e):D\to X$, and $h=d_A\mathcal L:D\to Y$. Whisker the counit square by $\mathcal LA$ using the composition/whiskering lemma. It gives $s_Xb_{M[r]}=b_M[r]s_D$. The basic-operation shift lemma gives the square for $d_A$; prewhisker by $\mathcal L$ using the same composition lemma to obtain $s_Yh_{M[r]}=h_M[r]s_D$. This uses naturality of $d_A$ at $s_{\mathcal L}$, rather than identifying $\mathcal L(M[r])$ with $\mathcal LM[r]$ by an equality.

proof.text: For tensor put $D(M,N)=\mathcal L(\mathcal R\mathcal LM\otimes^L\mathcal R\mathcal LN)$, $X(M,N)=\mathcal L(M\otimes^LN)$, $Y(M,N)=\mathcal LM\widehat\otimes^L\mathcal LN$, $b=b_T$ and $h=d_\otimes(\mathcal LM,\mathcal LN)$. In slot one factor $e_M\otimes e_N=(1_M\otimes e_N)(e_M\otimes1)$; the counit square handles the second factor, and naturality of the first-slot tensor shift at $e_N$ handles the first. Slot two uses the factorization $(e_M\otimes1_N)(1\otimes e_N)$, the counit square at $N$ and naturality at $e_M$. Apply $\mathcal L$ and its natural shift. These give $s_Xb_{[r]}=b[r]s_D$ in each slot. The basic-operation lemma's signed square for $d_\otimes$, precomposed in that slot with $\mathcal L$, gives $s_Yh_{[r]}=h[r]s_D$. All tensor naturality used here is for degree-zero derived morphisms; the second-slot comparison retains its specified Koszul sign.

proof.text: In either unary or tensor case the preceding $b$-square implies $s_Db_{[r]}^{-1}=b^{-1}[r]s_X$. Consequently $s_Ya_{[r]}=s_Yh_{[r]}b_{[r]}^{-1}=h[r]s_Db_{[r]}^{-1}=h[r]b^{-1}[r]s_X=a[r]s_X$. This is exactly the claimed insertion square. Naturality follows by the same multiplication of the naturality equations for $b,h$: inverses of natural isomorphisms are natural. No new comparison is selected.

proof.text: The basic-operation lemma supplies naturality and addition coherence for the operation shifts and for the total-limit shift on $\mathcal L$. Apply the adjunction-shift uniqueness lemma to the opposite adjunction $\mathcal L^{\rm op}\dashv\mathcal R^{\rm op}$, with shift functors $[a]^{\rm op}$ and the inverse-opposite comparisons; its unit and counit are $e^{\rm op},u^{\rm op}$, and its unit (counit) compatibility is the counit (unit) compatibility for $\mathcal R\dashv\mathcal L$. By its clause (iii) the mate comparisons on $\mathcal R$ fixed by the shift-data definition commute with the shift, are coherent for zero and addition, and are compatible with $u,e$. By its clause (ii) a comparison on $\mathcal R$ compatible with $u,e$ and the fixed $\mathcal L$-comparison is unique; the cochain reduction comparisons are such by the reduction/limit lemma, so they equal the mate comparisons. Hence the composite comparisons used above are the fixed shift data, also at $0$ and negative integers. Explicitly the second-slot coefficients multiply as $(-1)^{ri}(-1)^{si}=(-1)^{(r+s)i}$, and the cone diagonals as $(1,(-1)^r)(1,(-1)^s)=(1,(-1)^{r+s})$; both formulas hold for all integers. Pasting and inversion preserve the already coherent comparison equations. Shifting translates a common finite cohomological or Tor interval by $-r$, so the stipulated domains remain valid for each $r$. Zero objects and empty opens give the unique zero maps; $r=0$ gives the identity squares.
